John W. Campbell, The Black Star Passes.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/john-w-campbell/the-black-star-passes

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- John W. Campbell, the author and writer of the preface, died 1971 (Wikidata Q435056, P570 = 1971-07-11).

First publication of the text used: 1953 (SE colophon: 'The Black Star Passes was published in 1953 by John W. Campbell').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1953 (SE colophon), which is after 1930, so this bullet relies on Standard Ebooks' statement of rights quoted below.
- Country of origin (United States): the stories first appeared in the American magazines Amazing Stories and Amazing Stories Quarterly, and the book was first published in 1953 by Fantasy Press of Reading, Pennsylvania (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Black_Star_Passes; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_Press). The origin is the United States, the same country as the bullet above, so no other country's term applies.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
